title: Host memory observation
responsibility: Parses macOS or Linux memory counters, or reads Windows host totals, and returns total, available, and pressure facts; unsupported or invalid sources fail.

inputs.name: macMemory.text
inputs.description: `vm_stat` output parsed for a nonzero page size and the `Pages free`, `Pages inactive`, and `Pages speculative` counters. Missing or invalid values make the calculated available bytes non-finite and cause an error.
examples:
Mach Virtual Memory Statistics: (page size of 16384 bytes)
Pages free: 100.
Pages inactive: 200.
Pages speculative: 50.

inputs.name: macMemory.pressure
inputs.description: The raw `kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level` text consumed by `macMemory`. Whitespace is trimmed; `1`, `2`, and `4` map to `normal`, `warning`, and `critical`, and every other value maps to `unknown`.

inputs.name: macMemory.total
inputs.description: Physical-memory total in bytes passed to `macMemory`; it becomes `memoryTotalBytes` and caps calculated available bytes with `Math.min`. The function does not validate this value.

inputs.name: linuxMemory.text
inputs.description: Text parsed for `MemTotal` and `MemAvailable` in kB and converted to bytes. Missing or nonnumeric counters, or a nonpositive `MemTotal`, make `linuxMemory` throw.

outputs.name: macMemory
outputs.description: Memory result containing the supplied total, available bytes computed as page size times the free, inactive, and speculative page counts and capped at total, and mapped pressure. Pressure values outside `1`, `2`, or `4` become `unknown`.

outputs.name: linuxMemory
outputs.description: Memory result containing `MemTotal` and `MemAvailable` converted from kB to bytes. Pressure is `critical` only when available bytes divided by total bytes is below `0.05`; otherwise it is `normal`.

outputs.name: hostMemory
outputs.description: Promise resolving to total bytes, available bytes, and pressure read from the current platform: macOS counters, Linux `/proc/meminfo`, or Windows `totalmem()`/`freemem()`. It rejects if a probe rejects or the platform is unsupported.

errors.name: Invalid memory counters
errors.description: `macMemory` throws `Error('Cannot read macOS memory counters')` for a missing or zero page size, or a non-finite available-byte calculation. `linuxMemory` throws `Error('Cannot read Linux available memory')` when parsed counters are non-finite or `MemTotal` is not positive.

errors.name: Unsupported resource platform
errors.description: `hostMemory` throws `Error('Unsupported resource platform')` when `platform()` is not `darwin`, `linux`, or `win32`.

errors.name: Memory probe failure
errors.description: `hostMemory` rejects when either macOS `checked` command rejects or the Linux `/proc/meminfo` read rejects; the awaited failure reaches the caller.

errors.name: HostMemoryReadError
errors.description: `macMemory` throws `HostMemoryReadError('Cannot read macOS memory counters')` when its page size is absent or zero, or its available-byte calculation is non-finite. `linuxMemory` throws `HostMemoryReadError('Cannot read Linux available memory')` when parsed counters are non-finite or `MemTotal` is not positive. `hostMemory` throws `HostMemoryReadError('Unsupported resource platform')` for any platform other than `darwin`, `linux`, or `win32`, and propagates parser errors.
